chunks: With this chain of transmission, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah and Bukayr, the two sons of Aʿyan: they asked Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام about the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, so he called for a basin or a vessel containing water.
Then he described the wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله until he reached the end of what Allah, the Exalted, said.
“And wipe your heads and your feet up to the ankles.”

“So when he wipes part of his head or part of his foot (his two feet), from between the ankles to the end of the tips of the toes, that suffices him.” We said: May Allah set you aright, where are the two ankles? He said: “Here,” meaning the joint below the shin bone. So the two asked: What is this? He said: “This is the shin bone.”

Then he said, may Allah the Exalted support him: when the one performing wudu (ablution) finishes the wudu, he should say the supplication: “All praise belongs to Allah, Lord of the worlds. O Allah, make me among those who repent often, and make me among those who purify themselves.”

key_terms.الدُّعَاءَ: the supplication to be recited after completing wudu
key_terms.الْكَعْبَيْنِ: the two ankles, here explained as the foot joint below the shin bone
key_terms.الْمَفْصِلَ: the joint, identified as the location intended for the ankle
key_terms.عَظْمِ السَّاقِ: the shin bone, distinguished from the ankle joint
key_terms.وَ امْسَحُوا: wipe; the Quranic command concerning the head and feet in wudu
key_terms.وُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith explain wiping the feet and the location of the ankles in wudu?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of wudu (ablution) of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله and clarifies that wiping in wudu is over the head and feet, in connection with the Quranic wording. It also identifies the intended location of the ankles and concludes with a recommended du'a after completing wudu.
